newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican confirms papal envoy to visit Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Vatican confirms papal envoy to visit Cuba.

text.p: The Vatican confirmed on Thursday that its foreign minister, Archbishop Jean-Louis Tauran, will visit Cuba next month.
The prelate will be in the communist-ruled island from October 25 at the invitation of the Cuban government and local Roman Catholic Church authorities, a statement said.
Diplomatic sources in Havana told Reuters on Wednesday that the visit could pave the way for a meeting in Rome in November beween President Fidel Castro and Pope John Paul.
Thursday's statement made no mention of the possible meeting between the Pope and Castro in Rome and it was not clear if Tauran would meet the Cuban leader during his visit to Havana.

There has been speculation in recent weeks that the Pope could meet Castro if he travelled to Rome for a World Food Summit organised by the U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) from November 13 to 17.
Such a meeting would cap recent improvements in sometimes tense relations between the Church and the government in Cuba and could lead to an historic papal visit to the island.
Cuba is the only country in Latin America the Pope has not visited.
Diplomatic sources in Rome said that, if Castro did meet the Pope in November, he would probably invite him to visit Cuba, perhaps in 1997.
Cuban authorities began moving toward more relaxed relations with Christian churches in the early 1990s after years of tension following the 1959 revolution that brought Castro to power.
Membership in the Communist Party is no longer barred to the faithful and constitutional changes in 1992 outlawed religious discrimination in clearer terms.
Ties with the Catholic Church have remained strained at times, notably over several calls in recent years by the island's Catholic bishops for political change.
